title: Persistency Addition to SecureRate Default Renewal Rates — Deferred Fixed Annuities
content:
Ashgrove SecureRate contracts (Deferred Fixed Annuities) that have been left undisturbed earn a persistency addition on default renewal.

**Rule.** The renewal persistency addition is **0.15% (0.0015)** where the expiring guarantee period was the first since issue and no withdrawal has ever been taken from the contract, **0.10% (0.001)** where the expiring guarantee period followed an earlier renewal and no withdrawal was taken during it, and nothing otherwise.

The addition is made to the tier's current base rate; the default renewal rate including it is held at no less than the guaranteed minimum interest rate and rounded to four decimal places.

**Reading the records.** An expiring guarantee period that began on the issue date — the contract's surrender charge schedule start date is its issue date — was the first since issue. One that began on a later surrender charge schedule start date followed an earlier renewal; "during it" means from that start date on. Withdrawals are read from the contract's activity history.

| Expiring guarantee period | Withdrawals | Persistency addition |
|---|---|---|
| First since issue | None ever | 0.15% |
| First since issue | At least one at any time | Nothing |
| Followed an earlier renewal | None during the expiring period (earlier periods do not matter) | 0.10% |
| Followed an earlier renewal | At least one during the expiring period | Nothing |

*Worked case (hypothetical, current base rate 5.20%):* a first guarantee period with no withdrawal ever adds 0.15% to the current base rate of 5.20%.
